questions.question: What will come in place of ? to satisfy the equation : (√5-1)² = ?-2√5
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Expand the left side mentally using the formula (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab.

(√5 − 1)² = 5 + 1 − 2√5 = 6 − 2√5

Comparing 6 − 2√5 with ? − 2√5 directly gives ? = 6.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(√5 − 1)² = ? − 2√5

**Formula Used:**

(a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²

**Calculations:**

⇒ (√5)² − 2 × √5 × 1 + 1² = ? − 2√5

⇒ 5 − 2√5 + 1 = ? − 2√5

⇒ 6 − 2√5 = ? − 2√5

⇒ ? = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity (a + b)²

The square of a sum is given by (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b².

Difference of Squares

The product of the sum and difference of two terms is given by (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².

Properties of Surds

When a square root is squared, it results in the original number: (√a)² = a. Multiplication of surds follows √a × √b = √(ab).

questions.question: What will be the compound interest on a sum of Rs. 25,000 after 3 years at the rate of 10% p.a.?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The effective compound interest rate for 3 years at 10% p.a. is directly known to be 33.1%.

CI = 33.1% of Principal

CI = (33.1 / 100) × 25000

CI = 33.1 × 250 = 8275

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8,275.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹25,000

Rate (R) = 10% p.a.

Time (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)T

Compound Interest (CI) = A − P

 
 Compound Interest Progression 25,000 Year 0 27,500 Year 1 30,250 Year 2 33,275 Year 3 
 + ₹2,500 (10%) 
 + ₹2,750 (10%) 
 + ₹3,025 (10%) Total Compound Interest = 33275 − 25000 = ₹8,275 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Amount (A) = 25000 × (1 + 10/100)³

⇒ A = 25000 × (11/10)³

⇒ A = 25000 × (1331/1000)

⇒ A = 25 × 1331 = 33275

⇒ CI = 33275 − 25000 = 8275

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8,275.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CI vs SI Difference

For 2 years: Difference = P(R/100)²

For 3 years: Difference = P(R/100)²(3 + R/100)

Half-Yearly Compounding

If interest is compounded half-yearly, the Rate becomes R/2 and the Time period becomes 2T.

Rule of 72

A quick rule of thumb: the time taken to double an investment at compound interest is approximately 72 / R years.

questions.question: If the simple interest on a certain sum of money for 3 years at 6% per annum is ₹360, what would be the simple interest on the same sum for 5 years at 8% per annum?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective interest rate for case 1 = 3 × 6% = 18%

Effective interest rate for case 2 = 5 × 8% = 40%

Given 18% of Principal = ₹360

⇒ 1% of Principal = 360 ÷ 18 = ₹20

⇒ 40% of Principal = 20 × 40 = ₹800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI₁) = ₹360

Time (T₁) = 3 years, Rate (R₁) = 6% per annum

Time (T₂) = 5 years, Rate (R₂) = 8% per annum

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 Case 1
 3 years @ 6%

 

 

 
 SI = ₹360
 18% of Principal

 
 Case 2
 5 years @ 8%

 

 

 
 SI = ?
 40% of Principal

**Calculations:**

From Case 1, we can find the Principal (P):

⇒ 360 = (P × 6 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ 360 = (18 × P) ÷ 100

⇒ P = (360 × 100) ÷ 18

⇒ P = ₹2000

Now, we will calculate Simple Interest for Case 2 using the same Principal:

⇒ SI₂ = (2000 × 8 × 5) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = (2000 × 40) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = 80000 ÷ 100 = ₹800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Ratio Method

Since the principal is constant, Simple Interest is directly proportional to the product of Rate and Time. SI₁ ÷ SI₂ = (R₁ × T₁) ÷ (R₂ × T₂).

Amount in Simple Interest

Amount = Principal + Simple Interest. The formula becomes Amount = P(1 + RT ÷ 100).

Compound vs Simple Interest

For the first year, SI and CI are equal if calculated annually. From the second year onwards, CI will always be greater than SI for a given rate and principal.

questions.question: The decimal 0.875 is best classified as:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Any decimal number that terminates (has an end) is always a rational number.

0.875 terminates after three decimal places, meaning it can be written exactly as 875 ÷ 1000.

Since it can be expressed in p/q form where both are integers, it is directly classified as a rational number.

**∴ The correct answer is Rational Number.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The decimal number 0.875.

**Method Used:**

Let us verify the definitions of the options provided:

⇒ **Whole Number:** Non-negative basic counting numbers (0, 1, 2, 3, ...).

⇒ **Integer:** Whole numbers and their negative counterparts (..., −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, ...).

⇒ **Irrational Number:** A number that cannot be written as a simple fraction (non-terminating and non-repeating).

⇒ **Rational Number:** A number that can be written in the form p/q, where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Clearly, 0.875 is neither a whole number nor an integer because it has a fractional part.

⇒ Convert 0.875 to a fraction.

⇒ 0.875 = 875 / 1000

⇒ Simplify the fraction by dividing both numerator and denominator by their highest common factor, 125.

⇒ 0.875 = 7 / 8

⇒ Here, p = 7 and q = 8. Both are integers and the denominator q is not equal to zero.

⇒ Therefore, it perfectly fits the definition of a rational number.

**∴ The correct answer is Rational Number.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Real Numbers

Real numbers consist of both rational and irrational numbers. Every valid point on the standard number line represents a real number.

Repeating Decimals

Decimals that are non-terminating but repeating (like 0.333...) can also be expressed as fractions (1/3). They are strictly classified as Rational Numbers.

Irrational Numbers Example

Famous irrational numbers include π (≈ 3.14159...) and √2 (≈ 1.414...). Their decimal expansions never terminate and never repeat their patterns.

questions.question: A pyramid is inscribed inside a cube with edge 12 cm, sharing the base and apex at center of top. Find volume of pyramid.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a pyramid is inscribed in a cube sharing the same base and maximum height, its volume is exactly one-third of the cube's volume.

Volume of the inscribed pyramid = (1/3) × (Volume of cube)

⇒ V = (1/3) × a³ = (1/3) × 12³

⇒ V = (1/3) × 1728 = 576 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 576 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Edge length of the cube (a) = 12 cm

The pyramid and the cube share the same base, meaning the base of the pyramid is a square of side 12 cm.

The apex of the pyramid is at the center of the top face of the cube, so the height of the pyramid (h) equals the edge length of the cube = 12 cm.

 
 
• 
• 
 
 
 
• 
• 
• 
• 
 
 
 12 cm (Base Edge) h = 12 cm Apex 

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a pyramid = (1/3) × Area of base × Height

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of base = Side × Side

⇒ Area of base = 12 × 12 = 144 cm²

⇒ Volume of pyramid = (1/3) × 144 × 12

⇒ Volume of pyramid = 144 × 4

⇒ Volume of pyramid = 576 cm³

*(Note: The unit specified in the options contains a typographical error by stating cm². Volume is always measured in cubic units, cm³.)*

**∴ The correct answer is 576 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Prism vs Pyramid

A pyramid's volume is exactly one-third the volume of a prism (like a cube or cuboid) that possesses the exact same base area and height.

Slant Height of Pyramid

The slant height (l) of a square pyramid can be deduced using the right-angled triangle formed by the height, half the base edge, and the slant height itself: l = √(h² + (a/2)²).

Surface Area of Pyramid

Total Surface Area = Base Area + Lateral Surface Area. For a square-based pyramid, the Lateral Surface Area (LSA) equals 2 × a × l.

questions.question: A rectangular field has an area of 600 square meters. If its length were increased by 10 meters and its width decreased by 2 meters, the area of the field would remain the same. Find the original dimensions (length and width) of the field.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For such questions, the fastest method is to verify the given options.

Condition 1: L × W = 600 | Condition 2: (L + 10) × (W − 2) = 600

Check Option 3: L = 50, W = 12 ⇒ Area = 50 × 12 = 600.

New length = 50 + 10 = 60, New width = 12 − 2 = 10 ⇒ Area = 60 × 10 = 600.

Both conditions are completely satisfied by Option 3.

**∴ The correct answer is Length = 50 m, Width = 12 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let the original length of the rectangle be L meters and width be W meters.

Original Area = L × W = 600 ⇒ W = 600 ÷ L

New length = L + 10, New width = W − 2

 Original Field L W Area = 600 
 
 New Field L + 10 W − 2 Area = 600 L × W = (L + 10) × (W − 2) 

**Formula Used:**

Area of a rectangle = Length × Width

**Calculations:**

⇒ (L + 10) × (W − 2) = 600

⇒ LW − 2L + 10W − 20 = 600

Substitute LW = 600:

⇒ 600 − 2L + 10W − 20 = 600

⇒ −2L + 10W − 20 = 0

Dividing the equation by −2:

⇒ L − 5W + 10 = 0

Substitute W = 600 ÷ L into the equation:

⇒ L − 5 × (600 ÷ L) + 10 = 0

⇒ L − (3000 ÷ L) + 10 = 0

Multiplying the entire equation by L:

⇒ L² + 10L − 3000 = 0

Factorizing the quadratic equation:

⇒ L² + 60L − 50L − 3000 = 0

⇒ L(L + 60) − 50(L + 60) = 0

⇒ (L − 50)(L + 60) = 0

⇒ L = 50 or L = −60

Since the length cannot be negative, L = 50 m.

⇒ W = 600 ÷ 50 = 12 m.

**∴ The correct answer is Length = 50 m, Width = 12 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area and Perimeter of Rectangle

The Area is the product of its length and width (A = L × W). The Perimeter is the total length of its boundary (P = 2 × (L + W)).

Quadratic Equations

A quadratic equation is of the form ax² + bx + c = 0. The roots can be found using factorisation or the standard formula x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) ÷ 2a.

Solving Two Variables

When dealing with two unknown variables, you need exactly two independent linear or non-linear equations to determine their unique values.

questions.question: A garden is in the shape of a regular hexagon, each side 20 m. If 5% of it is occupied by a circular fountain, find the remaining area.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total area of regular hexagon = 6 × (√3 / 4) × (side)²

⇒ Area = 1.5 × 1.732 × 20² = 1.5 × 1.732 × 400 = 1039.2 m²

The circular fountain occupies 5% of the garden, leaving 95% empty space.

⇒ Remaining area = 0.95 × 1039.2 = 987.24 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 987.24 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of the regular hexagonal garden (a) = 20 m

Area occupied by the circular fountain = 5%

Standard value of √3 ≈ 1.732

**Formula Used:**

Area of a regular hexagon = (3√3 / 2) × a²

Remaining Area = Total Area − Occupied Area

 
 5% 95% Remaining Garden 
• 
• 
• 20 m 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Area of Hexagon = (3√3 / 2) × 20²

⇒ Total Area = (3 × 1.732 / 2) × 400

⇒ Total Area = 1.732 × 600 = 1039.2 m²

⇒ The remaining area will be (100% − 5%) = 95% of the total garden space.

⇒ Remaining Area = (95 / 100) × 1039.2

⇒ Remaining Area = 0.95 × 1039.2 = 987.24 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 987.24 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Regular Hexagon

A regular hexagon is naturally composed of 6 congruent equilateral triangles. Its total area can be computed as 6 × (√3 / 4)a², where 'a' is the uniform side length.

Inradius and Circumradius

For any regular hexagon with side 'a', the circumradius (R) exactly equals the side length (R = a), while its inscribed circle radius (r) is (√3 / 2)a.

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all interior angles for a regular hexagon is given by (n − 2) × 180° = (6 − 2) × 180° = 720°. This makes each individual interior angle exactly 120°.

questions.question: The weights of three friends are in the ratio 7:8:9. If each gains 5 kg, the new ratio becomes 12:13:14. What is the original weight of the heaviest friend?

The original weight ratio is 7 : 8 : 9 and the new weight ratio is 12 : 13 : 14.

Notice that each individual part has increased uniformly by exactly 5 units (12 − 7 = 5, 13 − 8 = 5, 14 − 9 = 5).

The original weight of the heaviest friend = 9 units = 9 × 1 = 9 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 kg.**

questions.question: A triangular field has side lengths in the ratio 2:3:4 and perimeter 72 m. What is the area?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sides = 16 m, 24 m, and 32 m (distributed from 2:3:4 ratio and 72 m total perimeter).

Semi-perimeter (s) = 72 ÷ 2 = 36 m.

Area = √(36 × (36−16) × (36−24) × (36−32)) = √(36 × 20 × 12 × 4)

Area = √34560 ≈ 185.9 m² ≈ 186 m².

**∴ The correct answer is 186 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of sides = 2 : 3 : 4

Perimeter = 72 m

 
 24 m 16 m 32 m 

**Formula Used:**

Heron's Formula: Area = √(s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c))

where s is the semi-perimeter: s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the sides of the triangle be 2x, 3x, and 4x.

⇒ Perimeter = 2x + 3x + 4x = 72

⇒ 9x = 72 ⇒ x = 8

⇒ The sides are: a = 2 × 8 = 16 m, b = 3 × 8 = 24 m, and c = 4 × 8 = 32 m.

⇒ Semi-perimeter (s) = 72 ÷ 2 = 36 m.

⇒ Area = √(36 × (36 − 16) × (36 − 24) × (36 − 32))

⇒ Area = √(36 × 20 × 12 × 4)

⇒ Area = √34560 ≈ 185.9 m²

⇒ Rounding to the nearest integer, Area ≈ 186 m².

**∴ The correct answer is 186 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Right Angled Triangle

The area is calculated as ½ × base × perpendicular height.

Equilateral Triangle

All three sides are equal. Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × a², where 'a' is the side length.

Isosceles Triangle

Two sides are equal. Area = (b ÷ 4) × √(4a² − b²), where 'a' is the equal side and 'b' is the base.

questions.question: The value of a machine depreciates 10% in the first year, 20% in the second year, and 30% in the third year. If the initial value was Rs. 10,000, what is its value at the end of 3 years?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Final Value = Initial Value × (100 − D₁)% × (100 − D₂)% × (100 − D₃)%

Final Value = 10000 × 90% × 80% × 70%

Final Value = 10000 × (9/10) × (8/10) × (7/10)

Final Value = 10 × 504 = 5040

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 5040.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Value of the machine = Rs. 10000

Rate of depreciation for 1st year (R₁) = 10%

Rate of depreciation for 2nd year (R₂) = 20%

Rate of depreciation for 3rd year (R₃) = 30%

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 − R₁/100) × (1 − R₂/100) × (1 − R₃/100)

 
 
• 
• 
• 10000 9000 7200 5040 −10% −20% −30% Initial Year 1 Year 2 Year 3 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Value after 1st year = 10000 − (10% of 10000) = 10000 − 1000 = 9000

⇒ Value after 2nd year = 9000 − (20% of 9000) = 9000 − 1800 = 7200

⇒ Value after 3rd year = 7200 − (30% of 7200) = 7200 − 2160 = 5040

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 5040.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value undergoes successive percentage changes of a% and b%, the net percentage change is given by (a + b + a×b/100)%. For depreciation, the values of a and b are taken as negative.

Constant Depreciation Formula

If the rate of depreciation is constant at R% per annum, the value after n years is calculated as Value = P × (1 − R/100)ⁿ.

Compound Growth vs Depreciation

The same successive multiplication principle applies to population growth or compound interest, where rates are added instead of subtracted: Final Value = P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ.

questions.question: An electronics dealer marks an item 60% above cost and offers a festival discount of 25%, plus a cashback of Rs. 300 on the final selling price. If he still makes a 10% profit, what is the cost price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100%.

Marked Price (MP) = 100% + 60% = 160%.

Selling Price (SP) after 25% discount = 160% × 0.75 = 120%.

Given the overall profit is 10%, Final SP = 100% + 10% = 110%.

Difference (Cashback) = 120% − 110% = 10% = Rs. 300.

Since 10% = Rs. 300 ⇒ Cost Price (100%) = Rs. 3000.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup = 60% above CP

Discount = 25%

Cashback = Rs. 300

Overall Profit = 10%

**Formula Used:**

MP = CP × (1 + Markup% ÷ 100)

SP = MP × (1 − Discount% ÷ 100) − Cashback

 
 
 
 +60% Markup 
 −25% Discount 
 −Rs. 300 Cashback 
 +10% Overall Profit CP 100% MP 160% SP 120% Final SP 110% 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) be x.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = x × (1 + 60 ÷ 100) = 1.6x

⇒ SP before cashback = 1.6x × (1 − 25 ÷ 100) = 1.6x × 0.75 = 1.2x

⇒ Final SP = 1.2x − 300

⇒ We also know that Final SP = CP × (1 + 10 ÷ 100) = 1.1x

⇒ Equating the two Final SP expressions:

⇒ 1.2x − 300 = 1.1x

⇒ 1.2x − 1.1x = 300

⇒ 0.1x = 300

⇒ x = 300 ÷ 0.1 = 3000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Formula for MP and CP Ratio

When profit and discount percentages are given (without any fixed monetary adjustments), MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

Successive Discount

When two consecutive discounts of x% and y% are given on an item, the equivalent single net discount percentage is (x + y − x × y ÷ 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

If a shopkeeper claims to sell goods at Cost Price but uses a false weight, his profit percentage is given by (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight × 100%.

questions.question: Athar can do a certain work in the same time in which Baban and Chetan together can do it. If Athar and Baban together could do it in 10 days and Chetan alone in 50 days, then Baban alone could do it in:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(10, 50) = 50 units.

Efficiency of (Athar + Baban) = 5 units/day, Chetan = 1 unit/day.

Since Athar = Baban + Chetan, replacing Athar gives: 2 × Baban + Chetan = 5.

2 × Baban + 1 = 5 ⇒ Baban's efficiency = 2 units/day.

Time taken by Baban alone = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Athar takes the same time as Baban and Chetan together.

⇒ Efficiency of Athar (A) = Efficiency of Baban (B) + Efficiency of Chetan (C)

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A + B
 10
 50
 50 ÷ 10 = 5
 
 

 C
 50
 50 ÷ 50 = 1
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = B + C

⇒ Combined efficiency: A + B = 5

⇒ Substituting A = B + C in the combined efficiency equation:

⇒ (B + C) + B = 5

⇒ 2B + C = 5

⇒ Since C's efficiency is 1:

⇒ 2B + 1 = 5 ⇒ 2B = 4

⇒ B = 2 units/day

⇒ Time taken by Baban alone = Total Work ÷ B's Efficiency = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 days

**∴ The correct answer is 25 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work using LCM

Total work is generally assumed as the LCM of all the given time periods. This makes the one-day work (efficiency) an integer value, making calculation easier.

Work & Wages

Wages are distributed in the direct proportion of the amount of work done by each individual. If they work for the same duration, wages are split in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Pipes & Cisterns

The core concept remains exactly the same as Time & Work, with the only difference being that a leak or emptying pipe has negative efficiency.

questions.question: A storage box is in the shape of a right rectangular prism with internal dimensions 50 cm × 40 cm × 30 cm. How many liters can it hold?

Total Surface Area of Cuboid

Important Capacity Conversions

1 m³ = 1000 liters and 1 liter = 1000 cm³.

questions.question: An alloy contains tin and copper in the ratio 5:3. A second alloy contains tin and copper in the ratio 3:1. What quantity of the first alloy must be mixed with 20 kg of the second alloy to produce a new alloy with tin and copper in the ratio 4:2?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the Alligation rule directly on the fraction of Tin in the alloys:

Fraction of Tin: Alloy 1 = 5/8, Alloy 2 = 3/4, Mixture = 4/6 = 2/3

Ratio of quantities = (3/4 − 2/3) : (2/3 − 5/8) = 1/12 : 1/24 = 2 : 1

Given 1 part (Alloy 2) corresponds to 20 kg.

So, 2 parts (Alloy 1) = 2 × 20 = 40 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of Tin to Copper in Alloy 1 = 5 : 3

Ratio of Tin to Copper in Alloy 2 = 3 : 1

Target Ratio of Tin to Copper in New Alloy = 4 : 2 = 2 : 1

Quantity of Alloy 2 = 20 kg

**Formula Used:**

Alligation method applied to fractions of a single component (Tin) in the mixtures.

 
• 
• 
• 
• Alloy 1 (5/8) Alloy 2 (3/4) Mix (2/3) 1/12 1/24 Ratio = 1/12 : 1/24 = 2 : 1 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Fraction of Tin in Alloy 1 = 5 ÷ (5 + 3) = 5/8

⇒ Fraction of Tin in Alloy 2 = 3 ÷ (3 + 1) = 3/4

⇒ Fraction of Tin in New Alloy = 4 ÷ (4 + 2) = 4/6 = 2/3

Applying the rule of alligation to find the required ratio of quantities:

⇒ Ratio of Alloy 1 to Alloy 2 = (3/4 − 2/3) : (2/3 − 5/8)

⇒ Ratio = (9/12 − 8/12) : (16/24 − 15/24)

⇒ Ratio = 1/12 : 1/24

⇒ Required Ratio = 2 : 1

We are given that the quantity of Alloy 2 used is 20 kg (which represents 1 unit in the ratio):

⇒ Quantity of Alloy 1 = 2 × 20 kg

⇒ Quantity of Alloy 1 = 40 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 40 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alligation Method

It is a rule used to quickly find the ratio in which two or more ingredients must be mixed to produce a specific desired average or concentration. It can be applied on percentages, prices, and component fractions.

Replacement Method

If a container holds x units of pure liquid and y units are taken out and replaced by water n times, the remaining quantity of pure liquid is given by x × (1 − y/x)ⁿ.

Multiple Mixtures

When combining multiple mixtures containing differing ratios of the same components, always evaluate the quantities by converting the component ratios into absolute fractional parts out of the whole before combining them.

questions.question: If sin A + cos A = √2 , then find sin³ A + cos³ A.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If sin A + cos A = √2, then A = 45° is the only valid angle in the primary interval.

Substitute A = 45° into sin³ A + cos³ A.

sin³ 45° + cos³ 45° = (1/√2)³ + (1/√2)³

⇒ 1/(2√2) + 1/(2√2) = 2/(2√2)

⇒ 1/√2 = √2 / 2

**∴ The correct answer is √2 / 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sin A + cos A = √2

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² + b² − ab)

sin² A + cos² A = 1

**Calculations:**

⇒ Squaring both sides of the given equation:

⇒ (sin A + cos A)² = (√2)²

⇒ sin² A + cos² A + 2 sin A cos A = 2

⇒ 1 + 2 sin A cos A = 2

⇒ 2 sin A cos A = 1

⇒ sin A cos A = 1/2

⇒ Now, we need to find the value of sin³ A + cos³ A

⇒ Using the algebraic identity for the sum of cubes:

⇒ sin³ A + cos³ A = (sin A + cos A)(sin² A + cos² A − sin A cos A)

⇒ Substitute the known values into the identity:

⇒ sin³ A + cos³ A = (√2) × (1 − 1/2)

⇒ sin³ A + cos³ A = √2 × (1/2)

⇒ sin³ A + cos³ A = √2 / 2

**∴ The correct answer is √2 / 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Trigonometric Identities

The primary foundational identity is sin² A + cos² A = 1. Other related identities include 1 + tan² A = sec² A and 1 + cot² A = cosec² A.

Algebraic Identities for Cubes

The formula for the sum of two cubes is a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² + b² − ab). The difference of two cubes is given by a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + b² + ab).

Maximum Value of Sine and Cosine Expressions

For any general trigonometric expression of the form a sin x + b cos x, the maximum value it can attain is √(a² + b²). In this specific case, 1 sin A + 1 cos A has a theoretical maximum of √(1² + 1²) = √2, which perfectly matches the given equation and confirms A = 45°.

questions.question: Are these lines y = 2x + 3 and y = -(1)/(2)x - 1 perpendicular?

options.text: Only if they intersect at origin

questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Compare the given line equations with the standard slope-intercept form y = mx + c.

Slope of the first line (m₁) = 2

Slope of the second line (m₂) = −1/2

Product of slopes = 2 × (−1/2) = −1

Two lines are perpendicular if the product of their slopes is −1, which is exactly the case here.

**∴ The correct answer is Yes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Equation of first line: y = 2x + 3

Equation of second line: y = −1/2x − 1

**Formula Used:**

Condition for two intersecting lines to be perpendicular: m₁ × m₂ = −1 (where m represents the slope).

questions.question: If sin x = cos(5x - 60°), then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When sin A = cos B, their angles are complementary, meaning A + B = 90°.

⇒ x + 5x − 60° = 90°

⇒ 6x = 150°

⇒ x = 25°

**∴ The correct answer is 25°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sin x = cos(5x − 60°)

**Formula Used:**

sin θ = cos(90° − θ)

**Calculations:**

⇒ cos(90° − x) = cos(5x − 60°)

Equating the angles on both sides:

⇒ 90° − x = 5x − 60°

⇒ 5x + x = 90° + 60°

⇒ 6x = 150°

⇒ x = 150° ÷ 6

⇒ x = 25°

**∴ The correct answer is 25°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angle Identities

For any angle θ, sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, and sec(90° − θ) = csc θ.

Supplementary Angle Identities

For any angle θ, sin(180° − θ) = sin θ, cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ, and tan(180° − θ) = −tan θ.

Important Trigonometric Values

sin 30° = cos 60° = 1 ÷ 2 | sin 45° = cos 45° = 1 ÷ √2 | sin 60° = cos 30° = √3 ÷ 2.

questions.question: Two angles are complementary. The measure of one angle is 10 degrees more than three times the measure of the other angle. What is the measure of the smaller angle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Complementary angles always sum up to 90°.

We can check the given options for the smaller angle directly.

If the smaller angle is 20°, the larger angle must be 90° − 20° = 70°.

Now verify the given condition: 3 × 20° + 10° = 60° + 10° = 70°.

Since this perfectly matches the larger angle, our assumption is correct.

**∴ The correct answer is 20°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The two angles are complementary (their sum is 90°).

The measure of one angle is 10° more than three times the other angle.

 
 
 
• 
• 
• 
 90° x 3x + 10° Complementary Angles: Sum = 90° 

**Calculation:**

Let the measure of the smaller angle be x.

Then, the measure of the larger angle = 3x + 10°

Since the angles are complementary, their sum must be equal to 90°.

⇒ x + (3x + 10°) = 90°

⇒ 4x + 10° = 90°

⇒ 4x = 90° − 10°

⇒ 4x = 80°

⇒ x = 80° ÷ 4

⇒ x = 20°

**∴ The correct answer is 20°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Supplementary Angles

Two angles are considered supplementary if the sum of their measures is exactly 180°.

Adjacent Angles

Two angles are adjacent when they have a common side and a common vertex (corner point), and do not overlap.

Linear Pair of Angles

A linear pair is a pair of adjacent angles formed by intersecting lines. The sum of a linear pair is always equal to 180°.

Vertically Opposite Angles

These are the angles opposite each other when two straight lines cross. Vertically opposite angles are always equal to each other.

questions.question: In a triangle ABC, if the angle bisectors of ∠B and ∠C intersect at point I, and ∠BIC=110°, what is the measure of ∠A?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any triangle where the internal angle bisectors meet at incenter I:

∠BIC = 90° + ∠A ÷ 2

⇒ 110° = 90° + ∠A ÷ 2

⇒ ∠A ÷ 2 = 20° ⇒ ∠A = 40°

**∴ The correct answer is 40°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
• 
• A B C I 
 110° 
 ? 

**Given:**

In ΔABC, angle bisectors of ∠B and ∠C intersect at point I.

∠BIC = 110°

**Formula Used:**

When the internal angle bisectors of two base angles of a triangle meet, the angle formed is:

∠BIC = 90° + ∠A ÷ 2

**Calculations:**

⇒ ∠BIC = 90° + ∠A ÷ 2

⇒ 110° = 90° + ∠A ÷ 2

⇒ ∠A ÷ 2 = 110° − 90°

⇒ ∠A ÷ 2 = 20°

⇒ ∠A = 20° × 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Incenter Properties

Formed by the intersection of internal angle bisectors. Subtended angle ∠BIC = 90° + ∠A ÷ 2.

Excenter Properties

Formed by the intersection of external angle bisectors. Subtended angle ∠BEC = 90° − ∠A ÷ 2.

Circumcenter Properties

Formed by the intersection of perpendicular bisectors. Central angle ∠BOC = 2 × ∠A.

Orthocenter Properties

Formed by the intersection of altitudes. Subtended angle ∠BHC = 180° − ∠A.

questions.question: Simplify: (sqrt{3}+sqrt{2})²
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For an algebraic expression of the form (√a + √b)², the direct result is (a + b) + 2√(ab).

Here, a = 3 and b = 2.

⇒ (3 + 2) + 2√(3 × 2)

⇒ 5 + 2√6

**∴ The correct answer is 5 + 2√6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(√3 + √2)²

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

**Calculations:**

⇒ (√3 + √2)² = (√3)² + 2 × √3 × √2 + (√2)²

⇒ (√3)² = 3

⇒ (√2)² = 2

⇒ 2 × √3 × √2 = 2√6

⇒ 3 + 2√6 + 2

⇒ 5 + 2√6

**∴ The correct answer is 5 + 2√6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square of a Difference

(a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b². This rule is used for expanding terms like (√3 − √2)².

Difference of Squares

(a + b)(a − b) = a² − b². This identity is most often used to rationalize denominators involving square roots.

Product of Square Roots

√a × √b = √(ab), provided both a and b are non-negative numbers.

⇒ TR = 12 cm
